# AlibreScript Playground

- The Playground is a browser-based editor for AlibreScript, so you can explore the scripting API without installing Alibre Design.
  - What it does
    - Gives you a code editor that understands AlibreScript and suggests what is available as you type.
    - Shows you the parameters a function takes, which saves digging through documentation.
    - Runs in the browser, so there is nothing to install.
    - Includes a quick reference and starter content to get you going.
  - Getting started
    - Open the hosted Playground at <https://stephensmitchell.github.io/AlibreScript-playground/>.
    - Start typing in the editor and use the quick reference when you need it.
    - To run it yourself, open `source/index.html` in a browser.
  - Where things live
    - `source/` holds the pages, styles, scripts, and starter content.
    - `documentation/` holds reference notes.
  - Good to know
    - This is a beta, so treat it as a place to learn rather than a production tool.
    - The Playground only explores the API, and it cannot change a real Alibre model.
  - Use it under the MIT License.
